findings.message: 'EMAIL' is not a grok pattern. Logstash refuses to compile an unknown name, so the filter never registers and EVERY line fails to parse - not just the ones this capture touches. Use a defined pattern: NUMBER or BASE10NUM for a decimal, HOSTNAME for a domain, NOTSPACE for anything without a space.

the pattern matches 5 of 10 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is '2026-10-15 15:06:10 1xHN22-00017D-0I => /var/mail/mail (root@mx1.corp.example) <nobody@corp.example> R=mail4root T=address_file'. Of the 3 patterns, the closest to it is '%{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601:timestamp} %{DATA:msgid} (<=|=>|Completed) (?:%{DATA:sender})? the probe injected 'b2558312fb0c' as host.hostname, but the parser put it in observer.hostname. Whatever the source calls that key, its value is host.hostname - that is what the probe did.
the probe injected 'root' as user.name, but the parser put it in client.user.name. Whatever the source calls that key, its value is user.name - that is what the probe did.
